name: Menocore

lead: Menocore is a fashion micro-trend built on loose knits, linen, tunics and neutral colors, described as inspired by middle-aged women on a low-key beach vacation [1].
The looks payoff is a comfortable, polished-but-unforced style. The name blends normcore with menopause, and the trend has been worn by women of many ages [1].

paras: People build outfits from palazzo trousers, linen jackets, bucket hats, tunics, mules and neutral tones [1].
No health risks; commentators have criticized the trend as reflecting a mainly white, affluent aesthetic [2].

angle.text: Followers dress in loose neutral pieces for a relaxed, understated look.

lead: Menocore is a fashion trend credited to Harling Ross of Man Repeller, described as the aesthetic of middle-aged women on a low-key beach vacation. The term merges normcore and menopause [1].

Typical pieces are loose knits, linen, bucket hats, tunics, blouses, flowy silhouettes and chunky sandals or mules. Meryl Streep in It's Complicated and Diane Keaton in Something's Gotta Give are cited as inspirations, and pre-menopausal women wear it too [1].

paras: The term appeared around 2017; a HuffPost piece on November 7, 2017 called it newly coined [2]. It riffs on normcore, a trend popularised in 2014 and meaning deliberately plain dress [3].
HuffPost contributor Habiba Alcindor argued the trend reflects a white, wealthy fantasy that overlooks women of color and that invisibility is not desirable to them [2].

timeline.event: HuffPost discusses the newly coined term [2].
Style press features menocore as a summer micro-trend [1].
